evidence: Read the brief and all three notes (1,696 words in total). The voice is one consistent requester, a small UK law firm that writes 'we/our' and gives its reasons, with no spec-table cadence. Reasons in context: instruction.md:1 'our clients keep emailing documents to whoever answered last'; conversations.md:5 'Our clients ask several things at once, so answers have to stay with their question'; conversations.md:9 'People fix typos and figures'; conversations.md:29 'Our internet in court is patchy.'; walls-and-retention.md:17 'because a leak is a professional-conduct problem for us'; walls-and-retention.md:19 'Conflicts come up mid-matter'; integration.md:7 'which is why we care that the order stays consistent'. Contractions appear throughout: doesn't and we'll (instruction.md:3,9), mustn't/can't/don't/I'm/I've (conversations.md:13,17,25,31), won't/don't/isn't/can't (integration.md:3,5,9), aren't (walls-and-retention.md:17). The British register (mustn't, 'all sorts') matches the UK firm and names. Sentence length varies, from short lines such as 'Two things matter more than anything else.' (instruction.md:3), 'Only a partner changes a timer.' (walls-and-retention.md:23) and 'Our internet in court is patchy.' to longer explanatory sentences. A grep for marketing or LLM tells (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|streamline|utiliz|furthermore|moreover|additionally|crucial|em-dash) found nothing. There are no bullet lists. The only table is the account table (walls-and-retention.md:5-11), which is necessary data rather than a parallel spec list. 'Must' appears only 4 times in plain speech, and 'shall' never appears. The voice of instruction.md and the notes is consistent: the same 'we', the same firm, and the same closing request 'Before you hand it over, please try it the way we'll use it' (instruction.md:9). The template instruction.md is a CHANGE_ME stub, so all of the prose is task-authored. The workbook's internal annotation for row 2 is empty. Minor observations, not defects: (a) conversations.md switches from the firm's 'we' to an individual 'I' at :25 and :31 ('When I open a matter', 'what I'm doing'). This reads as a natural person writing rather than a voice change between files. (b) Some passages are dense enumerations, such as the list of wall leak routes at walls-and-retention.md:17 and the transcript contents at :35. They still sit inside reasoned prose, and checklist shape belongs to row 1, not this row. (c) The workbook's 'occasional terse fragment' has few true examples, but short declaratives provide the terse register the row allows. Adversarial probe: an LLM-polished rewrite (headings plus parallel 'The system must...' bullets, 'seamless real-time collaboration') would fail this row, and these notes contain none of those markers. The broken-app and conforming-app framing does not apply because this row grades prose, not runtime. No runtime measurement is required for this row, so no missing evidence remains.
